extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers/applicants for new technology add-on payments, hospital administrators, coding and billing professionals, and other stakeholders responding to CMS NTAP rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural rules from CMS for evaluating and processing New Technology Add-On Payment (NTAP) applications for FY2027, including public-participation requirements, coding assignments, eligibility/documentation deadlines, and the substantive criteria (newness, cost, substantial clinical improvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public input before publication of a notice of rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(5)(K)(viii) requires providing, before publication of a proposed rule, for public input regarding whether a new service or technology represents an advance in medical technology that substantially improves diagnosis or treatment of Medicare beneficiaries; making public and periodically updating a list of services/technologies with pending add-on payment applications; accepting comments, recommendations, and data from the public; and providing, before publication, for a meeting where stakeholder organizations may present comments, recommendations, and data to CMS clinical staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS implemented this by publishing a Federal Register notice and holding a virtual New Technology Town Hall (recorded and posted online). CMS considered town hall presentations and written comments received by the deadline in its evaluation. The notice and meeting were focused specifically on the substantial clinical improvement criterion; comments unrelated to that criterion are not summarized in the proposed rule. CMS invites public comments on its proposals that relate to the items discussed at the town hall.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICD-10-PCS Section 'X' codes decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions regarding creation, deletion, or revision of ICD-10-PCS Section 'X' codes are handled in the same manner as other ICD-10-PCS code changes and are referred to the ICD-10 Coordination and Maintenance Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several technologies approved (or under consideration) for NTAP may be assigned Section 'X' codes; CMS posted ICD-10-PCS Guidelines (including Section 'X') on its website and encourages providers to review them. Coding changes follow established ICD-10-PCS coordination processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness determination and duration of NTAP eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A medical service or technology may continue to be considered 'new' for NTAP purposes within 2 or 3 years after the point when data begin to become available reflecting the inpatient hospital code assigned to the new service or technology. CMS's practice is to begin and end NTAPs on a fiscal-year basis and (for technologies first approved prior to FY2025) to use a 6‑month window before and after the start of the fiscal year and generally follow a guideline using the 3‑year anniversary and April 1 midpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning with technologies first approved for NTAP in FY2025 or later, CMS will extend NTAP for an additional fiscal year when the 3‑year anniversary of the product's entry onto the U.S. market occurs on or after October 1 of that fiscal year. For technologies first approved prior to FY2025 (and substantially similar technologies), CMS uses the midpoint of the upcoming fiscal year (April 1) to determine continued 'new' status. Tables in the rule list start dates, 3‑year anniversaries, coding, and proposed payment amounts for specific technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FDA marketing authorization date and handling of commercial availability delays
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS generally uses the FDA marketing authorization date as the indicator of when a technology begins to become available on the market and when data reflecting costs begin to become available; in specific circumstances CMS has recognized a later date where an applicant can prove a delay in actual availability after FDA approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to limit recognition of documented commercial availability delays to the period before the NTAP becomes effective. If a technology is not yet available for sale when its NTAP becomes effective, CMS would consider the newness period to begin on the September 30 preceding the start of the NTAP. CMS explained concerns that recognizing delays after NTAP becomes effective could allow applicants to postpone commercial availability indefinitely and undesirably extend NTAP duration (examples discussed include ZEVTERA® and SAINT Neuromodulation System).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions to distinguish devices/technologies when codes overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an ICD-10-PCS procedure code could identify more than one related device/technology (e.g., Ceribell Delirium Monitor System vs. Ceribell Status Epilepticus Monitor both linked to XX20X89), CMS may propose to exclude cases that report specific ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes (e.g., those identifying status epilepticus) in combination with the procedure code to isolate the population relevant to the NTAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes specific exclusions (see Table 10.2 in the rule) and invites public comment on excluding cases reporting certain ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes in combination with the procedure code for purposes of the NTAP for FY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility timing and documentation requirements (traditional pathway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for NTAP under the traditional pathway must have received FDA marketing authorization by May 1 of the year prior to the beginning of the fiscal year for which the application is being considered. For technologies not already FDA market authorized for the indicated use, applicants must have a complete and active FDA market authorization request at the time of NTAP application submission and must provide documentation of FDA acceptance or filing to CMS at the time of application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements implement regulations at §412.87(e) and (f). CMS posted online applications and supporting information (with exceptions for certain confidential/copyrighted information). Noncompliant applications (missing FDA authorization/documentation) are ineligible; some applicants withdrew before the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core statutory NTAP evaluation criteria: newness, cost, substantial clinical improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for NTAP, a technology must meet the statutory criteria of newness, cost, and substantial clinical improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS summarizes applicants' assertions regarding how a medical service or technology meets those criteria and, for technologies that have FDA marketing authorization, makes proposals to approve or disapprove each application. For technologies that have not received FDA authorization, CMS will not propose approval or disapproval because it will not determine substantial clinical improvement prior to FDA safety/effectiveness determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence expectations and common concerns for the substantial clinical improvement criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial clinical improvement requires evidence that the technology provides a treatment option for patients unresponsive to or ineligible for currently available therapies or improves clinical outcomes relative to existing technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expressed specific concerns that can undermine substantial clinical improvement claims: reliance on administrative claims data (cannot confirm medication ingestion or identify true prior treatment failure), short follow-up durations (e.g., average follow-up of 2.6 months may be inadequate), absence of direct comparative data to existing therapies, limitations of network meta-analyses (inconsistent statistical significance, lack of comparisons to all relevant comparators), post‑hoc analyses and posters offering limited support, and that claims about adherence/persistence require appropriate comparators and adequate time frames. CMS cites examples from the COBENFY™ application where such evidence gaps led to continued questions about whether the criterion is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing constraint: CMS will not assess substantial clinical improvement before FDA safety/effectiveness determination
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS has stated it does not believe it is appropriate to determine whether a medical service or technology represents a substantial clinical improvement before the FDA makes a determination as to whether the medical service or technology is safe and effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, CMS will not propose approval or disapproval of NTAP applications for technologies that have not yet received FDA marketing authorization for the indication at issue; this sequencing affects which applications are actionable in the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting, transparency, and summary format for NTAP applications
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS publicly posts online NTAP applications and supporting information beginning with FY2024 applications, with limited exceptions for cost/volume and confidential or copyrighted information. In the proposed and final rules, CMS provides more succinct summaries of applicants' assertions regarding how technologies meet newness, cost, and substantial clinical improvement criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS refers readers to the MEARIS public postings for detailed applicant materials and provides tables and concise summaries in rule preambles; CMS invites public comment on its proposals and on whether specific technologies meet criteria.
